in_hebrew.name: אובדוליה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אובדוליה נגזר מהמילים העבריות 'עבד' ו'אל', שפירושן משרתת אלוהים. הוא סימל את הקשר בין האדם לאלוהים, והוא נושא משמעות עמוקה של שירות ומסירות לאל.

in_greek.name: Ὀβδουλία
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Ὀβδουλία προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὶς ἑβραϊκὲς λέξεις 'עבד' καὶ 'אל', ποὺ σημαίνουν δοῦλος τοῦ Θεοῦ. Ἐκφράζει τὴν σχέση τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν καὶ φέρει βαθειὰ σημασία ὑπηρεσίας καὶ ἀφοσιώσεως εἰς τὸν Θεόν.

in_latin.name: Obdulia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Obdulia derivatur ex vocibus hebraicis 'עבד' et 'אל', quae significant servam Dei. Hoc nomen exprimit relationem hominis ad Deum et habet profundam significationem servitii et devotionis ad Deum.

in_english.name: Obdulia
in_english.meaning: Servant of God, worshipper of God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Obdulia originates from the Hebrew words 'עבד' (eved), meaning servant, and 'אל' (El), meaning God. It signifies a servant or worshipper of God, conveying a deep sense of service, devotion, and loyalty to God. Historically, the name has been used in Christian tradition to denote a person dedicated to serving God and living a life of spiritual devotion.

saint_reference.note: A 4th-century martyr and saint in the Christian tradition.

data.cultural_impact: The name Obdulia signifies loyalty, dedication, and service to God. It is a name that carries a rich history and association with Christian tradition and values. The name found its place in the Bible, which has greatly influenced Western culture and its literary works. It continues to inspire and uplift Christians today, serving as a reminder of the importance of faith and obedience to God.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Obdulia holds deep spiritual significance as it reflects the heart of a person who is devoted to God. This name embodies the Christian virtue of humility, as one who is obdulious is a servant of God. It evokes images of steadfastness, perseverance, and willingness to submit to God's will. Thus, the name Obdulia is a powerful reminder of the importance of faith and devotion in our spiritual lives.

historical_references.reference: Obdulia, the widow of Sanctus, was a pious and charitable woman in ancient Rome during the 3rd century AD. She was well known for her acts of kindness and generosity towards the poor and needy.

Saint Obdulia, a virgin and martyr of the early Christian Church, lived during the reign of Decius (249-253 AD). She was persecuted for her faith and, after being tortured, is said to have miraculously escaped death and was later beheaded.
